messages.subject: Using data.table with renjin
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to embed a number of already-written R libraries into a java program. Those libraries have dependencies on data.table.  The documentation at http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/data.table/1.9.6 says that “This package can be loaded by Renjin but there was an error compiling C/Fortran sources and all tests failed.” That suggests that using renjin for these R libraries is not going to be trivial. Is there any way, perhaps by pulling out the appropriate code and compiling it myself, that I can make the data.table available to renjin?

Hello,

I'm trying to run the following via renjin:

length(seq(from=Sys.Date(),to = some.date, by = 'month'))

I'm getting the following error:

Java exception thrown: org.renjin.sexp.DoubleArrayVector cannot be cast to org.renjin.sexp.IntVector

Any idea where the mismatch could be coming from?

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: Using data.table with renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jason,

great to see that you are giving Renjin a try and you are correct to note that the data.table package cannot be used in Renjin at this moment. The message that the package can be loaded simply means that we can load it's namespace without errors.

To be honest, the data.table package is on our list of package to render obsolete with Renjin so I don't expect Renjin to support the data.table package in the near future. The goal of Renjin is to improve the performance of the interpreter such that you do not need to resort to "workaround" packages like data.table, bigmemory, sqldf, etc. We are also of the opinion that the copy-by-reference semantics used by the data.table package do not belong in the R language.

My advise would be to keep your R libraries as simple as possible by keeping the dependencies to an absolute minimum. I would refactor the code that depends on the data.table package to only use R's base commands. I realize that this may be a lot of work, but it is currently your best option if you want to utilize the benefits of Renjin.

Maarten-Jan

P.S. BeDataDriven provides commercial support to companies who need their R code to run in a Java stack with Renjin, see http://www.renjin.org/support.html for details.

messages.subject: Re: How to use a library in renjin
messages.subject_clean: How to use a library in renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,
If you are embedding Renjin in a Java application, then the library's jar needs to be on the classpath.

You can find documentation on this here:
http://docs.renjin.org/en/latest/introduction.html#using-cran-packages-in-renjin

Please note that it looks like the clv package is not completely compatible, check packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org> for details.

Alex
